summary: Steel fire tower on Pine Mountain near Warm Springs, built 1930 as a memorial gift; no source found says whether it stands today.

events.note: Work began 14 Sept 1930 under two Georgia State Forestry men, with Meriwether County supplying labor.
Dedicated 8 Dec 1930 with an address by Gov. Franklin D. Roosevelt of New York; a tablet to Charles L. Davis was unveiled.
An April 1931 Atlanta Constitution caption describes watchmen in the tower using a telescope to locate fires.

evidence.supports: Tower is a steel fire tower built on Pine Mountain near Warm Springs; construction began 14 Sept 1930
evidence.quote: Work began today on the construction of a steel fire tower at a point on Pine Mountain near Warm Springs, known as 'The View.'

evidence.supports: Date of the Macon Telegraph report
evidence.quote: September 14, 1930

evidence.supports: Planned height of 80 feet and fire area covered
evidence.quote: This tower will be 80 feet high and will be used for the fire area in Meriwether, Harris and Talbot counties.

evidence.supports: Supervision by two state forestry men; labor from Meriwether County
evidence.quote: This tower is being constructed under the supervision of H. M. Sebring and Jack Thurmond, of the Georgia State Forestry department. The labor is furnished by Meriwether county.

evidence.supports: Courthouse at Greenville visible from the ground
evidence.quote: the view is so excellent that standing on the ground one can easily see the courthouse at Greenville with the naked eye.

evidence.supports: Tower donated by Georgia Wilkins in memory of Charles L. Davis; the 1930 report says donated to Meriwether County
evidence.quote: This structure was donated to Meriwether county by Miss Georgia Wilkins, of Columbus, in memory of the late Charles L. Davis of Warm Springs, an uncle of Miss Wilkins.

evidence.supports: Gov. Franklin D. Roosevelt of New York gave the dedication address
evidence.quote: Gov. Franklin D. Roosevelt of New York yesterday delivered an address dedicating the first fire watch tower

evidence.supports: Dedication on 8 December 1930
evidence.quote: The tower was dedicated on December 8 by Gov. Franklin D. Roosevelt.

evidence.supports: A tablet to Charles L. Davis was unveiled with the dedication
evidence.quote: With the dedication of the tower, a tablet to the memory of Charles L. Davis, one-time owner of the Georgia Warm Springs properties, was unveiled.

evidence.supports: Atlanta Constitution caption: gift to the Warm Springs Foundation (conflicts with the 1930 county donation)
evidence.quote: The tower is a gift to the Warm Springs Foundation from Miss Georgia Wilkins, a niece of the late Charles L. Davis, pioneer citizen of Meriwether county.

evidence.supports: January 1931 Forest Worker item dates the Forest Worker report
evidence.quote: January 1931

evidence.supports: Forest Worker calls Davis for many years owner of the Warm Springs property
evidence.quote: for many years owner of the Warm Springs property.

evidence.supports: NPS names a Charles Davis as builder of the Meriwether Inn at Warm Springs in 1893 (not confirmed as the same man)
evidence.quote: In 1893, Charles Davis constructed the Victorian 300-room Meriwether Inn

evidence.supports: Telescope mounted on the tower in April 1931, for fire watching and visitors
evidence.quote: A powerful telescope, which will be used in watching for forest fires and for observation purposes by visitors, who flock to Warm Springs, has been mounted on the Charles Lamar Davis Memorial tower there.

evidence.supports: April 1931 date of the telescope report
evidence.quote: April 16, 1931

evidence.supports: Atlanta Constitution caption: watchmen locate forest fires for many miles; tower called the Charles Lamar Davis memorial fire tower
evidence.quote: In the tower watchmen, with the aid of a powerful telescope, can locate forest fires for many miles around.

evidence.supports: Tower called the Charles Lamar Davis memorial fire tower, 80 feet
evidence.quote: Above is the Charles Lamar Davis memorial fire tower rising 80 feet above the surrounding country.

evidence.supports: Georgia lookout list places Davis Memorial in Meriwether County with the Georgia Forestry Commission
evidence.quote: Meriwether County - Georgia Forestry Commission

evidence.quote: GA071,Davis Memorial Lookout Tower, 32.87596,-84.69020 ,Meriwether,1245

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Evening Star item dated 9 December 1930 says the address was given 'yesterday', and The Forest Worker says 8 December. Both point to 8 December 1930.

sources.title: Davis Memorial, Eastern US Lookouts (quoting The Macon Telegraph, Evening Star, The Forest Worker, Butler Herald and The Atlanta Constitution, 1930-1931)

notes_for_editor: 1930-31 history rests on newspaper extracts as reproduced by the lookout site; I read those quotes on that page, not the newspapers. Nothing found on current condition, access, staffing or ownership today. UNRESOLVED: recipient of the gift (Meriwether County per the Macon Telegraph, Sept 1930; Warm Springs Foundation per an Atlanta Constitution caption, Apr 1931); the story reports both. The brief record says ownership 'state' (from the Eastern US Lookouts entry), but no source read says the tower is state-owned; the 1930-31 sources name the county or the foundation. The NPS Charles Davis (1893 inn) is not confirmed as the Charles Lamar Davis the tower honors. Brief record checks out on county, elevation (1,245 ft = 379.5 m) and agency; no corrections proposed.
